meta.name: Specialty PA test set
meta.note: All patients and charts are synthetic. Criteria come from public payer policies (links and versions below). Policy text is not reproduced here; the model receives the policy document itself.

case_types.clean: Meets criteria. Tests for false alarms.
case_types.gap: Something the policy requires is missing or doesn't count.
case_types.drug_layer_trap: Dose, units, product or timing is wrong in the request as drafted.

severity_levels.decision_changing: Would produce a wrong approval or a denial.
severity_levels.delay: Would trigger a pend or a request for more information.
severity_levels.false_alarm: Flags a problem that isn't there. Costs reviewer time.

actions.submit: Criteria met and request is correct as written.
actions.pend_for_info: Get missing documentation or attestation from the prescriber before submitting.
actions.fix_request: Change product, code or dose before submitting.

cases.case_note: Commercial Aetna plan. Medical benefit, IV induction.
cases.chart: GI clinic note, 10/20/2026. Synthetic patient SK, 34-year-old female. Ileocolonic Crohn's disease diagnosed 03/2024. Current: 6 to 8 loose stools per day, crampy abdominal pain, 3 kg weight loss over 2 months. CDAI 310. Colonoscopy 09/2026: deep ulcers in terminal ileum and ascending colon. CRP 18 mg/L; fecal calprotectin 640 mcg/g. Weight 64 kg. Prior therapy: mesalamine 4.8 g/day for 6 months (11/2025 to 05/2026), inadequate response. No corticosteroids, no immunomodulators, no prior biologic or targeted synthetic drug. QuantiFERON-TB Gold negative 10/02/2026. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative. Assessment: moderately to severely active ileocolonic Crohn's disease without complications. Plan: start risankizumab-rzaa 600 mg IV at weeks 0, 4 and 8, then subcutaneous maintenance from week 12. Prescriber: board-certified gastroenterologist.
cases.request_as_drafted: Skyrizi 600 mg IV at weeks 0, 4, 8. Dx: Crohn's disease of small and large intestine.
cases.trap: Aetna has no prior-therapy requirement for Crohn's. A model that asks for a failed conventional therapy is raising a false alarm.
cases.rationale: CPB 1009 Crohn's criteria: moderately to severely active CD; prescribed by or with a gastroenterologist. 'Other' section: TB evaluation before initiation; no concurrent biologic or targeted synthetic for the same indication. All documented. Dosing per label. J2327 = 1 mg per unit.

cases.case_note: Commercial UnitedHealthcare plan that applies the policy's medical necessity criteria.
cases.request_as_drafted: Skyrizi 600 mg IV at weeks 0, 4, 8. Dx: Crohn's disease of small and large intestine. Prior therapy: failed mesalamine.

missing_or_problems: No failure of a listed conventional therapy (corticosteroid, 6-mercaptopurine, azathioprine or methotrexate) and no prior systemic targeted immunomodulator. Mesalamine is not on the policy's list.

cases.trap: The request says 'failed mesalamine,' which looks like it satisfies a prior-therapy rule. UHC's list doesn't include mesalamine.
cases.rationale: 2026D0116H medically necessary criteria, Crohn's IV: failure of a conventional therapy at up to maximally indicated doses (corticosteroids such as prednisone, methylprednisolone, budesonide; 6-MP; azathioprine; methotrexate) unless contraindicated, OR prior FDA-approved systemic targeted immunomodulator for CD. Also GI prescriber, labeled induction dosing, 3 induction doses authorized. Ask the prescriber for any steroid or immunomodulator history or a documented contraindication.

cases.case_note: Commercial Cigna plan, pharmacy benefit. Same patient profile as S1, but in this version she was on Skyrizi before.
cases.chart: GI clinic note, 10/22/2026. Synthetic patient SK, 34-year-old female. Ileocolonic Crohn's disease diagnosed 03/2024. Treatment history: risankizumab-rzaa 600 mg IV induction 01/2025 to 03/2025, then 360 mg SC every 8 weeks 04/2025 to 02/2026, with clinical remission (CDAI under 150). Stopped 02/2026 when insurance coverage lapsed. Enrolled in Cigna plan 09/2026. Symptoms returned: 5 loose stools per day, abdominal pain, CDAI 280, CRP 12 mg/L. Plan: 'Restart Skyrizi 360 mg SC every 8 weeks via on-body injector.' No plan for IV induction documented. Prescriber: gastroenterologist.
cases.request_as_drafted: Continuation of therapy: Skyrizi 360 mg SC every 8 weeks. Patient previously achieved remission on Skyrizi.

answer_key.product: Skyrizi (risankizumab-rzaa) 360 mg/2.4 mL prefilled cartridge with on-body injector
missing_or_problems: Patient is restarting therapy, so initial criteria apply, not continuation.
Initial criteria need a prescriber attestation that the patient will receive Skyrizi IV induction within 3 months of starting Skyrizi SC. Not documented.

cases.trap: The office drafted it as a continuation because the patient responded before. Cigna reviews restarting patients under initial criteria.
cases.rationale: IP0670 p. 3: Crohn's initial approval (6 months) requires age over 18, prescriber attestation that the patient will receive Skyrizi IV induction within 3 months of initiating Skyrizi SC, and GI prescriber. Continuation requires being established on therapy for at least 6 months plus response; a patient restarting therapy is reviewed under initial criteria.

cases.chart: GI clinic note, 10/15/2026. Synthetic patient IF, 29-year-old male. Ileal Crohn's disease diagnosed 06/2023. Weight 80 kg. Prednisone 40 mg taper over 8 weeks (03/2025 to 05/2025) with flare at the end of the taper. Azathioprine 200 mg daily (2.5 mg/kg; TPMT activity normal) since 01/2026. Despite 9 months of azathioprine: 6 stools per day, abdominal pain, CDAI 290, CRP 22 mg/L; MR enterography 09/2026 shows 25 cm of active terminal ileal inflammation without stricture or fistula. No prior biologic or targeted synthetic drug. QuantiFERON-TB Gold negative 10/01/2026. Assessment: moderately to severely active ileal Crohn's disease without complications, failed corticosteroids and azathioprine. Plan: start infliximab-dyyb (Inflectra) 5 mg/kg = 400 mg IV at weeks 0, 2 and 6, then every 8 weeks. Continue azathioprine. Prescriber: gastroenterologist.
cases.request_as_drafted: Inflectra 400 mg IV at weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks. Dx: Crohn's disease of small intestine.
cases.trap: Two false-alarm chances: flagging azathioprine as a disallowed combination (the policy bars combining with a targeted immunomodulator, not with azathioprine), or miscounting units.
cases.rationale: 2026D0004AR: Inflectra and Avsola are preferred. Crohn's initial: moderately to severely active CD; failure of one conventional therapy (corticosteroids, 6-MP, azathioprine, methotrexate) or high-risk disease or prior targeted immunomodulator; FDA-labeled dosing; not combined with a systemic targeted immunomodulator; GI prescriber; initial authorization up to 12 months. Q5103 = 10 mg per unit, so 400 mg = 40 units (exactly four 100 mg vials).

cases.case_note: Commercial Aetna plan, medical benefit. For this case, assume the plan applies CPB 0341 with no separate preferred-product program.
cases.chart: GI clinic note, 10/27/2026. Synthetic patient IF2, 45-year-old female. Colonic Crohn's disease diagnosed 2022. Weight 60 kg. Current: 7 bloody stools per day, CDAI 300, colonoscopy 10/2026 with extensive colonic ulceration. Budesonide 9 mg daily 08/2026 to 10/2026 without response. No prior biologic or targeted synthetic drug. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative 10/2026. No tuberculosis screening on file. Plan: start infliximab-dyyb (Inflectra) 5 mg/kg = 300 mg IV at weeks 0, 2 and 6, then every 8 weeks. Prescriber: gastroenterologist.
cases.request_as_drafted: Inflectra 300 mg IV at weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks. Dx: Crohn's disease of large intestine.

missing_or_problems: No documented negative TB test (skin test or interferon-release assay) within 12 months for a biologic-naive member.

cases.trap: Everything else in the chart is strong, which makes the missing TB test easy to skip.
cases.rationale: CPB 0341 Crohn's: moderately to severely active CD; GI prescriber; no prior-therapy requirement. Biologic-naive members need a documented negative TB test (skin test or IGRA) within 12 months of starting. No concurrent biologic or targeted synthetic. Q5103 = 10 mg per unit, 300 mg = 30 units.

cases.chart: Identical to I1, except the plan line reads: 'Plan: start infliximab (Remicade) 5 mg/kg = 400 mg IV at weeks 0, 2 and 6, then every 8 weeks. Continue azathioprine.'
cases.request_as_drafted: Remicade 400 mg IV at weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks. Dx: Crohn's disease of small intestine.

answer_key.product: Inflectra (infliximab-dyyb) or Avsola (infliximab-axxq) instead of Remicade
missing_or_problems: Remicade is non-preferred. It needs a 14+ week trial of Inflectra or Avsola with minimal response plus attestation, or an intolerance, contraindication or adverse event. None documented.

cases.trap: Clinical criteria are fully met, so a model may approve the product as written.
cases.rationale: 2026D0004AR pp. 1-2: Inflectra and Avsola preferred; Remicade and Renflexis non-preferred with the trial or intolerance requirement. J1745 = infliximab excluding biosimilar, 10 mg per unit; Q5103 Inflectra and Q5121 Avsola are 10 mg per unit.

cases.case_note: Commercial Cigna plan with weight loss coverage, pharmacy benefit.
cases.chart: Primary care note, 10/28/2026. Synthetic patient ZB, 41-year-old female. Height 165 cm, weight 85.5 kg, BMI 31.4. Hypertension on lisinopril. Never treated with a GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonist. Enrolled in a structured lifestyle program (dietitian visits and behavioral counseling) since 06/2026, following a reduced-calorie diet, weight down 1.5 kg. Plan: start tirzepatide (Zepbound) 2.5 mg SC weekly for 4 weeks, then 5 mg weekly; continue reduced-calorie diet and program.
cases.request_as_drafted: Zepbound 2.5 mg SC once weekly, 4 single-dose pens per 28 days. Dx: obesity, BMI 31.4, hypertension.
cases.trap: None by design. Tests for false alarms, such as demanding 6 months of lifestyle program (another payer's rule) or prior oral drugs.
cases.rationale: IP0816 pp. 4-5: age 18+; at least 3 months of behavioral modification and dietary restriction; baseline BMI 30+ (or 27+ with comorbidity), measured before any GLP-1; used with behavioral modification and reduced-calorie diet. Initial approval 8 months. Policy p. 2: 2.5 mg weekly is the starting dose, for initiation only.

cases.case_note: Commercial Aetna plan that applies policy 6947-C, pharmacy benefit.
cases.chart: Primary care note, 10/30/2026. Synthetic patient ZB2, 38-year-old male. Height 174 cm, weight 100 kg, BMI 33.0. Dyslipidemia on atorvastatin. Never treated with a weight-loss medication. Joined employer-sponsored weight management program (nutrition coaching, activity plan, monthly follow-up visits) in 08/2026; 3 months completed. Plan: start tirzepatide (Zepbound) 2.5 mg SC weekly; continue program.
cases.request_as_drafted: Zepbound 2.5 mg SC once weekly, 4 single-dose pens per 28 days. Dx: obesity, BMI 33.0, dyslipidemia. Patient participating in weight management program.

missing_or_problems: Policy requires participation in a comprehensive weight management program with continuing follow-up for at least 6 months before starting drug therapy. Only 3 months documented.

cases.trap: Three months of a lifestyle program is enough for Cigna (Z1). A model that carries that over will approve this one.
cases.rationale: 6947-C (P04-2025): adults; baseline BMI 30+ or 27+ with a weight-related comorbidity; comprehensive weight management program with continuing follow-up for at least 6 months before starting drug therapy. Initial approval 8 months. The posted page's quantity limit table lists 'Tirzepatide (Brand Mounjaro)' in every row (2 mL, 4 pens, per 21 days for a 28-day fill), not Zepbound. Flagged by the model in run 1. Pend for any earlier program participation; otherwise resubmit once 6 months are documented.

cases.case_note: Commercial Cigna plan with weight loss coverage, pharmacy benefit.
cases.chart: Identical to Z1, except the plan line reads: 'Plan: start tirzepatide (Zepbound) 5 mg SC weekly; continue reduced-calorie diet and program.'
cases.request_as_drafted: Zepbound 5 mg SC once weekly, 4 single-dose pens per 28 days. Dx: obesity, BMI 31.4, hypertension.

answer_key.dose: 2.5 mg (not 5 mg) for the first 4 weeks
missing_or_problems: Starting dose should be 2.5 mg weekly for initiation, then 5 mg at week 4. The request starts at 5 mg in a GLP-1-naive patient.

cases.trap: Coverage criteria are met, so a model may submit the 5 mg request as written.
cases.rationale: IP0816 p. 2: starting dose 2.5 mg SC once weekly, for initiation only; 5 mg at week 4; maximum 15 mg. Coverage criteria pp. 4-5 met as in Z1. Confirm the dose with the prescriber before submitting.
